references.text: The people hung on Jesus and listened to him speak in the temple. Luke 19:48 tells us that all the people were hanging on him and listening to him, which is directly parallel to the people coming early in the morning to hear him in the temple.

The preceding verse, Luke 21:37, describes Jesus' daily routine of teaching in the temple during the day and spending nights on the Mount of Olives, forming the direct context for the people's early arrival.

John 8:1-2 describes a very similar situation: Jesus went to the Mount of Olives in the evening, and early in the morning he came again to the temple, and all the people came to him, and he sat down and taught them.
Mark 11:17-18 tells of Jesus' teaching in the temple and that the crowd was amazed at his instruction, showing the same pattern of the people gathering to hear him.

Matthew 21:17 tells us that Jesus left the city in the evening and went to Bethany to spend the night, which corresponds to the pattern Luke describes of Jesus leaving the city at night and then returning to the temple.
Luke 22:39 confirms that it was Jesus' custom to go to the Mount of Olives, consistent with the daily pattern described here.

The psalmist seeks God early in the morning: Psalm 63:2 expresses the same eagerness to seek God early, just as the people came early to hear Jesus. The Greek verb ὀρθρίζω (to come early in the morning) reflects this longing.
Luke 5:1 describes how the crowd pressed in on Jesus to hear the word of God, showing the recurring theme in Luke's Gospel of the people's eagerness to listen to Jesus' teaching.
